notes: Approved provider/model routes and billable tool services for commercial inference. This file is a policy gate, not a model catalog: a route is usable only when every requirement below passes, and the requirements are deliberately redundant. (1) Provider-side transport flags pinned per request: zdr true, data_collection deny, allow_fallbacks false, require_parameters true, provider only/order set to the single approved provider slug. (2) Account-side operator verification, because provider ZDR alone is not sufficient: prompt/completion logging must be disabled on the account and free models need a separate training opt-out. (3) A pinned https endpoint and pinned maximum prices, so spend is bounded without fetching a live price at request time. (4) A dated approval plus a dated operator review with recorded evidence. Tool services carry their own ceiling and review and are deny-by-default. As shipped, nothing is approved and no default route is set: that is the intended steady state until an operator has verified every condition for a specific route.

routes.notes: Carried over from the pre-entitlements tier configuration and intentionally left unqualified. To approve: verify availability; pin the transport block above to the exact provider slug with zdr true, data_collection deny, allow_fallbacks false, require_parameters true; record that account-level prompt/completion logging is disabled and that free models are excluded from training; set max price ceilings in microusd per 1M prompt/completion tokens; then set approved true with an approval_expires_at, and record an operator_review with reviewer, evidence and review_expires_at.

tool_services.notes: Not approved. Deny-by-default: a tool service that is absent from this list, or present but unqualified, must not be callable, so an unconfigured service cannot become a bypass around the route rules.
